public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 119

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/119](https://www.erdosproblems.com/119)
- [Be91] Beck, J., The modulus of polynomials with zeros on the unit circle: A problem of Erdős.
  Annals of Math. (1991), 609-651.
- [Er57] Erdős, Paul, Some unsolved problems. Michigan Math. J. (1957), 291-300.
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, Some unsolved problems. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er64b] Erdős, P., Problems and results on diophantine approximations. Compositio Math. (1964),
  52-65.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved. (1982), 59--79.
- [Er90] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite unsolved problems. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990),
  467-478.
- [Er97f] Erdős, Paul, Some unsolved problems. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge,
  1993) (1997), 1-10.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
- [Li77] Linden, C. N., The modulus of polynomials with zeros on the unit circle. Bull. London Math.
  Soc. (1977), 65--69.
- [Va99] Various, Some of Paul's favorite problems. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul Erdős
  and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999).
- [Wa80] Wagner, Gerold, On a problem of Erdős in {D}iophantine approximation. Bull. London Math.
  Soc. (1980), 81--88.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Finset Set

namespace Erdos119

/-
Here we use 0-indexing for generality and convenience, while in the original problem
formulation 1-indexing was used. This change does not affect the meaning of the problem.
In the description of the problem below we remain faithful to the original one.
-/

/-- Let $z_i$ be an infinite sequence of complex numbers such that $|z_i| = 1$ for all $i \geq 1$.
For $n \geq 1$ let $p_n(z) = \prod_{i \leq n} (z - z_i)$. -/
noncomputable def p (z : ℕ → ℂ) (n : ℕ) : ℂ → ℂ :=
    fun w => ∏ i ∈ range n, (w - z i)

/-- Let $M_n = \max_{|z| = 1} |p_n(z)|$. -/
noncomputable def M (z : ℕ → ℂ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    sSup { (‖p z n w‖) | (w : ℂ) (_ : ‖w‖ = 1) }

/--
Is it true that $\limsup M_n = \infty$?

This is Problem 4.1 in [Ha74] where it is attributed to Erdős.

The weaker conjecture that $\limsup M_n=\infty$ was proved by Wagner [Wa80], who show that there is
some $c>0$ with $M_n>(\log n)^c$ infinitely often.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1268917deaaaa0d674f651287027baa26cea9920/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos119.lean#L1759"]
theorem erdos_119.parts.i :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ (z : ℕ → ℂ) (hz : ∀ i : ℕ, ‖z i‖ = 1),
      atTop.limsup (fun n => (M z n : EReal)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true that there exists $c > 0$ such that for infinitely many $n$ we have $M_n > n^c$?

The second question was answered by Beck [Be91], who proved that there exists some $c>0$ such that
$\max_{n\leq N} M_n > N^c$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1268917deaaaa0d674f651287027baa26cea9920/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos119.lean#L1712"]
theorem erdos_119.parts.ii :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ (z : ℕ → ℂ) (hz : ∀ i : ℕ, ‖z i‖ = 1),
      ∃ (c : ℝ) (hc : c > 0), Infinite {n : ℕ | M z n > n ^ c} := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true that there exists $c > 0$ such that, for all large $n$, $\sum_{k \leq n} M_k > n^{1 + c}$?

The \$100 prize was offered for the third question in [Er97f]. This was resolved by GPT 5.6 and
Korsky (see the proof claims), who proved that $\sum_{k\leq n}M_k \gg \frac{n^{5/4}}{\sqrt{\log n}}$
(and hence for infinitely many $n$ we have $M_n> n^{1/4-o(1)}$).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1268917deaaaa0d674f651287027baa26cea9920/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos119.lean#L1687"]
theorem erdos_119.parts.iii :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ (z : ℕ → ℂ) (hz : ∀ i : ℕ, ‖z i‖ = 1),
      ∃ (c : ℝ) (hc : c > 0), ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
        ∑ k ∈ range n, M z k > n ^ (1 + c) := by
  sorry

end Erdos119

reformulations.difference: The file indexes the sequence from 0: `p z n w = ∏ i ∈ range n, (w - z i)`. So for k ≥ 1, `M z k` is the source's M_k for the sequence z_i^src = z (i-1). There is also an extra value `M z 0 = 1` (empty product), which the source does not define. The Lean sum `∑ k ∈ range n, M z k` therefore equals 1 + ∑_{k=1}^{n-1} M_k: it includes the M_0 = 1 term and omits M_n. The source's sum is ∑_{k≤n} M_k = ∑_{k=1}^{n} M_k. This looks like an off-by-one at first sight.
reformulations.equivalence_argument:
For any nonnegative sequence a, (∃ c>0, eventually ∑_{k<n} a_k > n^{1+c}) ↔ (∃ c>0, eventually ∑_{k=1}^{n} a_k > n^{1+c}).

(→) Keep the same c. We have ∑_{k=1}^{n} a_k = ∑_{k<n+1} a_k − a_0 > (n+1)^{1+c} − a_0. Since (n+1)^{1+c} − n^{1+c} ≥ (n+1)^c, this is ≥ n^{1+c} once (n+1)^c > a_0.

(←) Use c/2. We have ∑_{k<n+1} a_k ≥ ∑_{k=1}^{n} a_k > n^{1+c} = n^{c/2}·n^{1+c/2}. Once n^{c/2} ≥ 2^{1+c/2}, this is ≥ (2n)^{1+c/2} ≥ (n+1)^{1+c/2}. Then shift n.

Apply this with a = M z (M ≥ 0 via `Real.sSup_nonneg`), under ∀ z. I proved it in Lean as `Erdos119.iii_equiv`. Its right-hand side uses `∑ k ∈ Icc 1 n, M z k`, which is exactly the source's sum after reindexing z. The proof depends only on the standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).

The same 0-indexing in parts.i and parts.ii only adds the index n = 0. That cannot change a limsup, or whether {n | M z n > n^c} is infinite.

review.notes:
I found no misformalization. All three declarations state the three questions on erdosproblems.com/119. Each has answer(True), which matches the source: (i) proved by Wagner; (ii) answered by Beck, whose zbMATH review gives absolute constants c, c0 > 0 with max_{n≤N} M_n > c0·N^c for all N and all sequences; (iii) resolved by Korsky with GPT-5.6. The `research solved` tag matches the site's 'SOLVED (LEAN)' and the teorth database's 'solved (Lean)'.

Definitions:
- `M` is an `sSup` over a nonempty, bounded set (the image of the compact unit circle), so it is the true maximum. Checked in Lean: `M z 0 = 1` and `M (fun _ => 1) 1 = 2`.
- The limsup in part (i) is taken in `EReal`, so `= ⊤` really means "unbounded". It avoids the ℝ junk value.
- `n ^ c` elaborates to `(↑n : ℝ) ^ c` (rpow).
- `Infinite ↑{n | …}` is equivalent to `Set.Infinite`.

Quantifier order: in the file, c may depend on the sequence (∀ z ∃ c). This matches the source's wording: "Let z_i be … Is it true that there exists c>0 …". The known results (Beck; Korsky) give absolute constants, so the stated answer True holds under either reading.

formal_proof records: I downloaded the linked plby/lean-proofs file at the cited commit and renamed its namespace. I compiled it under this repository's toolchain (Lean v4.33.1 / Mathlib v4.33.1): exit 0, no sorry. The external `p` and `M` are definitionally equal to the repository's (`funext; rfl`). Bridge theorems proved the exact types of `erdos_119.parts.i/ii/iii`, checked with `type_of%`, using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The cited lines (L1759 parts.i, L1712 parts.ii, L1687 `erdos_119`, aliased as parts.iii) are the right declarations.

Minor, non-mathematical: the parts.iii docstring quotes an older version of the site's remark (∑ M_k ≫ n^{5/4}/√log n, hence M_n > n^{1/4−o(1)}). That is the proof claim the site accepted in July 2026. The page as last edited on 1 Sep 2026 states the improved bound ∑_{k≤n} M_k ≫ n^{3/2−o(1)}, hence M_n > n^{1/2−o(1)}. Both statements are true, so the mathematics is unaffected; the docstring could optionally be updated.

I could not get Erdős's original [Er97f] text, but the file cites erdosproblems.com's wording, and I checked against that.
